name: Gnocchi Burro e Salvia
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Wash and dry the unpeeled potatoes, prick them a few times, and bake on a tray for 50–60 minutes until a skewer slides easily through the centre. Baking keeps the flesh drier than boiling, so the gnocchi need less flour.

Cool the potatoes for 10–15 minutes until safe to touch but still warm. Split, scoop out the flesh and press through a ricer onto a clean work surface; discard the skins. Spread briefly to release steam, then sprinkle with 4 g salt and most of the flour.

Bring the potato and flour together gently with a scraper. Add the remaining flour only as needed to make a soft dough that holds together; do not knead hard or the gnocchi will be chewy. Divide into eight pieces, roll each into a rope about 2 cm thick and cut into 2 cm pillows. Roll over fork tines for shallow ridges if desired.

Bring the measured water to a gentle boil in a wide pot and add 6 g salt. Cook the gnocchi in three or four batches without crowding. After they float, simmer for about 1 more minute; cut one to check that the middle is hot and no raw flour remains. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain briefly.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Add dry sage leaves and swirl for 3–4 minutes, until the butter turns nut brown and smells toasted and the sage is crisp, not burnt. Immediately lower the heat and add the cooked gnocchi; toss gently for 1 minute to coat.
Add black pepper and taste before using the remaining 2 g salt. Divide into four warm bowls, pour over the browned butter and sage, and finish with grated vegetarian hard cheese. Serve immediately.
tips: Warm, dry potatoes make a light eggless dough. Use only enough flour to hold the gnocchi together, and watch the butter continuously once it starts browning.
passiveTime: Cool the baked potatoes for 10–15 minutes, until safe to handle but still warm.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
